system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

Hiring Team
Quillstone Payments
Application: Machine Learning Engineer - Customer Support AI
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer - Customer Support AI role at Quillstone
Payments. I bring six years in analytics and data science, including over four years building
models and experiments at Thistlebox. As I move towards machine learning engineering, I
offer practical experience with models used in business operations, strong Python and
statistical skills, and a disciplined approach to evaluating whether a model delivers useful
results.
At Thistlebox, I built a weekly recipe-level demand forecasting model using LightGBM and
calendar features. Operations uses it to order ingredients; forecast error (WAPE) fell from
23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also built an XGBoost churn
propensity model for targeting retention offers and validated uplift with a holdout. These
projects demonstrate feature engineering, model evaluation and the ability to connect
predictive performance with operational outcomes, all relevant to your team’s work on
support AI.
Alongside modelling, I write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the
analytics layer. I design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests each year for growth and
product teams, built the team’s sequential testing calculator, and present results to leadership
monthly. This combination of data preparation, experimentation and communication would
support collaboration with your backend engineers, data scientists and product managers,
particularly when assessing model accuracy and the effectiveness of support automation.
Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get answers quickly gives this role a clear measure of
practical value. Your emphasis on ownership, pragmatism and sharing context aligns with the
way my work connects analysis to decisions made by operations, product teams and
leadership. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my applied machine learning
experience and statistical foundation could contribute to your Customer Operations AI team.
Yours sincerely,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
